# Protein Intake Calculator

> A free, privacy-friendly protein intake calculator that tells you exactly how many grams of protein to eat per day based on your body weight, activity level and goal (muscle gain, fat loss, maintenance or athletic performance). All calculations run in the browser using evidence-based formulas (Mifflin–St Jeor for calories; g/kg protein ranges used by dietitians and strength coaches). No data is stored.

## Key facts

- General health (sedentary): 0.8–1.0 g of protein per kg of body weight per day.
- Weight loss (preserve muscle in a deficit): 1.6–2.2 g/kg.
- Muscle gain: 1.7–2.2 g/kg, combined with resistance training and a slight calorie surplus.
- Athletic / endurance performance: 1.8–3.1 g/kg.
- Per meal: aim for 25–40 g of protein across 3–4 meals for steady muscle protein synthesis.
- Women: same weight-based ranges as men; pregnancy and breastfeeding add ~25 g/day; post-menopause 1.4–1.8 g/kg to protect bone and muscle.
- Older adults (60+): often need 1.0–1.2 g/kg (1.2–1.5 g/kg in illness or recovery) to offset age-related muscle loss (sarcopenia).
- Teenagers: 0.85–1.0 g/kg for growth; teen athletes 1.2–1.6 g/kg from food first.
- On GLP-1 medications (Ozempic, Wegovy, Mounjaro): appetite drops, so prioritize protein first at each meal and target the higher end of the range.
- Type 2 diabetes with healthy kidneys: 1.0–1.5 g/kg supports satiety and steadier glucose; kidney disease requires individualized targets.
- Timing: total daily intake matters most; the post-workout "anabolic window" spans roughly 2 hours before to 2 hours after training.
- Protein shakes: a convenience, not a requirement — 1–2 shakes/day (~25–30 g per scoop) to fill the gap left by whole foods.

## Main pages

- [Protein Intake Calculator (English)](https://www.proteinintakecalculators.online/en): Interactive calculator plus guidance on daily protein needs by weight, goal and life stage.

## Topic guides (English)

- [Protein for weight loss](https://www.proteinintakecalculators.online/en/protein-for-weight-loss): Why 1.6–2.2 g/kg preserves muscle and controls hunger during a calorie deficit.
- [Protein for muscle gain](https://www.proteinintakecalculators.online/en/protein-for-muscle-gain): 1.6–2.2 g/kg with resistance training and a calorie surplus, spread across 3–4 meals.
- [Protein for women](https://www.proteinintakecalculators.online/en/protein-for-women): Weight-based ranges by life stage, including pregnancy and menopause.
- [Protein on Ozempic / Wegovy](https://www.proteinintakecalculators.online/en/protein-on-ozempic-wegovy): Hitting protein targets when GLP-1 medication reduces appetite.
- [High-protein foods list](https://www.proteinintakecalculators.online/en/high-protein-foods): Protein content of common foods (chicken, eggs, Greek yogurt, paneer, lentils, tofu, tuna, whey).
- [Protein by body weight](https://www.proteinintakecalculators.online/en/protein-by-body-weight): Daily gram targets for common body weights, general and active.
- [Vegetarian & vegan protein](https://www.proteinintakecalculators.online/en/vegetarian-vegan-protein): Same targets, plant- and dairy-based sourcing.
- [Protein for men](https://www.proteinintakecalculators.online/en/protein-for-men): Ranges for sedentary, muscle gain, fat loss and over-50 men.
- [Protein for seniors](https://www.proteinintakecalculators.online/en/protein-for-seniors): 1.0–1.2 g/kg after 60, anabolic resistance and sarcopenia prevention.
- [Protein for teenagers](https://www.proteinintakecalculators.online/en/protein-for-teenagers): Growth-stage needs and food-first guidance for teen athletes.
- [Protein during pregnancy](https://www.proteinintakecalculators.online/en/protein-during-pregnancy): ~1.1 g/kg in the second and third trimesters and while breastfeeding.
- [Best time to eat protein](https://www.proteinintakecalculators.online/en/best-time-to-eat-protein): Timing, per-meal distribution and the anabolic window, evidence-based.
- [Protein shakes per day](https://www.proteinintakecalculators.online/en/protein-shakes-per-day): How many shakes make sense and when powder is (not) needed.
- [Protein for diabetics](https://www.proteinintakecalculators.online/en/protein-for-diabetics): Blood-sugar-friendly protein targets and kidney-disease caveats.
- [Protein deficiency signs](https://www.proteinintakecalculators.online/en/protein-deficiency-signs): Symptoms of low protein intake and how to fix them.
- [FAQ](https://www.proteinintakecalculators.online/en#faq): Common questions on daily needs, per-meal amounts, GLP-1 medications, older adults and safety.

## Languages

Available in English (en), Spanish (es), French (fr), German (de), Portuguese (pt), Italian (it), Dutch (nl) and Arabic (ar) at https://www.proteinintakecalculators.online/{lang} — every topic guide exists in all eight languages with localized URLs (see the sitemap at https://www.proteinintakecalculators.online/sitemap.xml).

## Notes

This calculator provides general fitness guidance and is not a substitute for professional medical or nutritional advice.
